question: In a busy hospital, what percentage of the total waste produced is actually regular, non-hazardous household waste?
explanation: Most of what hospitals throw away is everyday rubbish (like paper and food packaging) that doesn't carry any infection risks. Only a small fraction is dangerous clinical waste! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: Which of these items counts as pathological waste?

options.B: An empty plastic intravenous fluid bag
options.D: A used hypodermic needle and syringe

explanation: Pathological waste refers to body parts, tissues, or organs removed during surgery or autopsies. Neat to know for clinical sorting! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: What is the biggest danger to waste handlers when sharps accidentally get mixed into ordinary trash bags?
explanation: Loose needles can easily poke through regular bags and skin, putting anyone handling the trash at risk of injury and infection. Always watch your sharps! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h2)

question: How can pouring leftover drugs down open drains harm our environment?

options.A: It triggers severe volcanic activity near water bodies
options.B: It contributes to antimicrobial resistance and harms aquatic life
options.C: It instantly freezes local rivers and kills vegetation
options.D: It causes immediate radioactive contamination in the soil

explanation: Drugs in our waterways expose local water animals and bacteria to medications, helping drug-resistant superbugs grow faster. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h2)

question: Which global health body leads the way in setting standards for medical waste management?
explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) provides the main guidelines and handbooks that countries follow to keep medical waste disposal safe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: Why do international health authorities want every country to have clear national policies on medical waste?

options.A: To ensure uniform taxation of hospital supplies
options.B: To establish legal accountability and standardize safe handling practices
options.C: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment
options.D: To replace local hospital management boards with global inspectors

explanation: National rules give hospitals the legal backing and clear steps they need to handle dangerous materials safely every single day. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: At what point in your clinical workflow should healthcare waste be sorted?

options.B: During the weekly municipal garbage collection
options.C: After transport to the central landfill
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Always sort waste right where you use it! Doing it immediately stops dangerous items from getting mixed up with regular trash. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: You just gave an injection on a busy ward. What is your very next step with that used needle?

options.A: Recap the needle carefully and place it in the regular paper bin
options.B: Throw the syringe into the general black bin bag
options.C: Leave the syringe on the bedside table for the cleaning staff
options.D: Drop the uncovered needle directly into a rigid safety box

explanation: Never recap needles! Drop them straight into a puncture-proof safety box to protect yourself and others from accidental pokes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: What main technology does an autoclave use to make infectious medical waste safe?
explanation: Autoclaves use intense steam pressure to hit temperatures that wipe out germs and pathogens on medical items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why is incineration the go-to method for body parts and human tissues?

options.A: It completely destroys anatomical parts safely and respectfully through high heat
options.B: It turns biological tissues into safe fertilizer for crops
options.C: It allows tissues to be recycled into new plastic products
options.D: It is the cheapest way to produce electricity

explanation: High-heat incineration is a safe, hygienic way to dispose of anatomical waste while treating human remains with proper dignity. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why are nurses considered the heartbeat of safe hospital waste management?

options.A: They design and build medical incinerators
options.B: They purchase all hospital waste disposal bags
options.C: They generate and supervise the sorting of the majority of clinical waste
options.D: They write national environmental protection laws

explanation: Because nurses carry out most bedside procedures, your daily choices make or break how well hospital waste gets sorted! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h6)

question: What is an important way nurses can guide patients and visitors regarding ward waste?

options.A: Revising the hospital's annual financial budget
options.B: Teaching them how to operate surgical autoclaves
options.C: Explaining the correct use of color-coded waste bins
options.D: Training them to administer intravenous injections

explanation: Visitors often toss things into the nearest bin. Taking a second to guide them helps keep our color-coded waste streams pure! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h6)

question: What is a major challenge for proper waste management in clinics with limited resources?

options.C: Shortages of proper segregation supplies and erratic electricity

explanation: Lack of steady power and basic items like safety boxes can make sticking to textbook waste rules tough in everyday rural practice. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h7)

question: If your rural clinic runs out of official safety boxes, what is a safe, clever backup plan for used needles?

options.A: Using locally available, puncture-resistant rigid containers
options.B: Throwing loose needles directly into the regular dustbin
options.C: Burying uncapped needles in the hospital garden
options.D: Washing and reusing disposable needles for multiple patients

explanation: Improvise safely! Using a sturdy, thick local container keeps everyone safe from needle pricks until official disposal arrives. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h7)
